context: Behavior evaluation only. Assume fresh successful routing selections unless a case says otherwise. Describe the chosen native or external execution path and tool arguments; no case authorizes launching delegates. Evaluate model, thinking, access, permissions, session continuity, and cache handling. External examples must use the guarded acpx_agent command from show with named persistent sessions.

evals.name: named-shortcut-triggers
evals.prompt: agptx - take a look at the retry logic in internal/queue/dispatch.go and tell me whether the backoff can starve the DLQ writer
evals.expected_output: Load the skill, resolve agptx, and use a matching native child when available; otherwise ensure a named persistent session and prompt it through guarded external acpx.
expectations: Loads the acpx delegation skill from the shortcut token 'agptx' alone, without the user naming acpx

Uses the resolved model with one thinking increment, preferring a compatible native child; external fallback ensures a named session and uses acpx --agent <guarded command> prompt -s <name> -f <prompt file>
Writes the read-only constraint into the prompt text rather than relying on --non-interactive-permissions deny to enforce it
Names internal/queue/dispatch.go explicitly in the prompt instead of expecting the delegate to glob for it
Plans to audit the run's tool calls afterward and report any write

evals.name: second-opinion-picks-default-gpt
evals.prompt: i've been staring at this migration plan for an hour and i think it's fine but i want another model to poke holes in it before i commit to it
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on the second-opinion intent with no shortcut named, and selects agpt as the default delegation.
expectations: Loads the acpx delegation skill without the user naming acpx or a shortcut
Selects agpt as the default second-opinion lane rather than asking the user to pick one
Does not escalate straight to agptx before agpt has been tried
Keeps the delegation read-only

evals.name: prose-rewrite-routes-to-pgpt
evals.prompt: this README intro reads like a press release, can you get it cleaned up properly rather than doing it yourself
evals.expected_output: Select pgpt or its alias agptw for prose and provide the writing-for-humans guidance.
expectations: Selects pgpt or agptw for prose; both resolve to the next lower capability tier at default thinking
Passes ~/.agents/plugins/plugins/core/skills/writing-for-humans/SKILL.md to the delegate along with the draft
Names the writing-for-humans path explicitly, because --add-dir roots are readable by exact path but not discoverable by glob

evals.name: write-flag-authorizes-edits
evals.prompt: /utils-agent:acpx -m aopus -w port the remaining callers in cmd/ off the deprecated NewClient signature
evals.expected_output: The explicit write flag authorizes the delegate to edit; permission flags do not grant that authority.
expectations: Parses -m aopus and -w from the invocation
Omits the read-only constraint from the prompt text because -w was supplied
Launches an external run with --approve-all because -w was supplied, instead of --non-interactive-permissions deny
Does not treat the acpx permission flags as the thing that granted write access
Does not require a disposable worktree, since the user authorized edits in the working checkout

evals.name: passthrough-instead-of-new-flags
evals.prompt: kick off a long review with afable, keep it in a session called review so i can ask follow-ups, and give it half an hour
evals.expected_output: Session name and timeout reach acpx through the -- passthrough rather than through invented skill flags.
expectations: Uses a named session because follow-up prompts must preserve context
Passes -s review and --timeout 1800 (or equivalent) through to acpx rather than inventing --session or --timeout skill flags
Uses external acpx sessions ensure --name review, then prompt -s review -f <prompt file>; global flags precede the subcommand and no exec invocation is used

evals.name: read-only-claim-is-honest
evals.prompt: have agpt review the diff on this branch. it must not touch any files - this checkout has uncommitted work i can't lose No compatible native subagent is available.
evals.expected_output: The model states that acpx permission flags do not prevent writes for these adapters, offers a disposable worktree to narrow the blast radius, and does not call that containment.
expectations: Does not claim --non-interactive-permissions deny, --deny-all, --no-terminal, or a permission policy will prevent the delegate from writing

Offers a disposable git worktree under --cwd for an uncommitted-work checkout while saying plainly that --cwd is only the working directory and nothing in acpx bounds where an ungated delegate can write
Puts the read-and-report-only constraint into the prompt text
Commits to auditing the log's tool calls and reporting any write that happened

evals.name: command-surface-question-goes-to-acpx-cli
evals.prompt: my ~/.acpx directory is getting huge. how do i clear out the closed sessions and their event streams from more than a month ago?
evals.expected_output: This is an acpx command-surface question, not a delegation. It belongs to the acpx-cli skill.
expectations: Does not load the acpx delegation skill, or loads it only to hand off
Answers from the acpx command surface with `acpx sessions prune --older-than 30 --include-history`
Does not select a shortcut or build a delegation invocation

evals.name: model-named-question-delegates-then-acts-locally
evals.prompt: ask the opus model whether this SQL index will actually get used, and then update the migration if it won't
evals.expected_output: Naming a model is a delegation request. The question goes to aopus read-only; the current session applies the migration change itself once the answer is back.
expectations: Selects aopus for the question rather than answering it in the current session
Keeps the delegation read-only: the delegate answers, it does not edit the migration
Plans to make the migration change locally after the delegate's answer, not to hand the edit to the delegate

evals.name: native-fable-review
evals.prompt: Get a Fable review of this diff. This Claude session exposes a native Agent tool whose Fable alias is verified to match the resolved afable concrete model and default thinking under our subscription.
evals.expected_output: Use the native Agent tool with task guidance and read-only constraint; no acpx launch or pane.
expectations: Resolves afable before launch
Uses native Agent with the matched model/default and task packet
Does not start acpx or a shared pane
Waits for the result and verifies the selected model

evals.name: native-inheritance-is-not-default
evals.prompt: agpt: review this patch. The cache selects Astra at its medium default. The parent is running high; native child tools can select Astra but always inherit high and cannot override effort.
evals.expected_output: Use guarded external acpx because the available native tool cannot honor default thinking.
expectations: Does not treat inherited high as the medium default
Uses the same cached Astra model via external acpx
Does not downgrade model or select a paid API

evals.name: machine-cache-refresh
evals.prompt: pgpt: review this patch. The machine cache expired. agent_clis includes only cursor-agent. Its catalog descriptions clearly identify a strongest GPT and a newer workhorse in the next lower capability tier.
evals.expected_output: Refresh through the calling model, select both from Cursor evidence, commit snapshot-bound choices, then resolve pgpt.
expectations: Uses the declared Cursor catalog, not an installed undeclared Codex
Interprets capability descriptions without a maintained model ranking
Commits snapshot-bound decision with reason and sources
Uses default thinking for pgpt and no metered API

evals.name: stale-cache-no-paid-fallback
evals.prompt: agpt: review this patch. Refresh failed temporarily; the last successful same-configuration selection is three days old. OpenRouter advertises a stronger paid model but no paid override was given.
evals.expected_output: Use the last successful selection with --allow-stale, report its age, and carry the guard flag into launch.
expectations: Reports three-day stale selection
Uses --allow-stale within seven-day grace
Does not select or launch the paid OpenRouter model
Stops if the cached route cannot run

evals.name: single-task-keeps-session
evals.prompt: Use agpt externally for a quick one-off review of this diff. I do not have a session name in mind. We are in Orca with a terminal handle.
evals.expected_output: Allocate a unique named ACP session, ensure it, and send the prompt through acpx-pane. Keep and report the session for follow-ups.
expectations: Chooses a task-specific unique session name even though the request says one-off
Uses the guarded command and same cwd for sessions ensure and prompt -s; stops if ensure fails
Uses acpx-pane for the prompt and does not use exec or an unnamed default session
Reports the session name and leaves it available after completion; closing the Orca viewer does not close the ACP session
Requires created true and the exact cwd and record identity before the first prompt; captures lastRequestId in a fresh post-prompt snapshot even on failure

evals.name: follow-up-keeps-conversation
evals.prompt: Ask agpt a follow-up about its review. The earlier task recorded session acpx-review-auth.ABC123, cwd /tmp/review-worktree, and its guarded agent command. The route and saved model/thinking still match. Our current cwd is a different checkout.
evals.expected_output: Verify and reuse the recorded session scope, with a new per-prompt log and prompt file.
expectations: Uses session acpx-review-auth.ABC123, cwd /tmp/review-worktree, and the recorded guarded agent command
Checks closed false, exact cwd/command/name, saved acpxRecordId, model/thinking, and acpSessionId before and after the follow-up
Stops if the expected session is absent rather than creating a context-free replacement
Uses prompt -s with fresh prompt/log files and snapshots; no ensure, new, model/configuration overrides, unrelated name, or exec

evals.name: session-model-mismatch
evals.prompt: Continue the review in the existing named session review using agptx. The refreshed routing selection now specifies a different model and effort from the saved session.
evals.expected_output: Report the mismatch and leave the saved conversation intact.
expectations: Compares the requested selection with the saved session before prompting
Does not claim refreshing the route changed the existing session's model or effort
Does not silently reuse the mismatched session, replace it with a new session, or fall back to exec

evals.name: lost-observer-active-turn
evals.prompt: The Orca pane vanished during an agpt review. Its saved receipt identifies the session and interrupted request. The queue owner is alive, and session watch shows that request started but has no turn_result yet.
evals.expected_output: Recover the saved scope and observe the existing request without submitting duplicate work.
expectations: Restores the saved session, cwd, guarded command, and backend ID before recovery
Uses sessions show, status, and history/events; distinguishes queue-owner health from turn completion
Runs sessions watch as a managed background task, optionally with a saved cursor; retains its handle and stops that watcher after the target turn_result or terminal watcher error
Does not submit a new prompt, create a replacement session, or equate closing the watcher with cancellation

evals.name: lost-answer-already-complete
evals.prompt: The shell waiting for an afable review died. The session receipt still matches, and its interrupted request has a successful turn_result with a retained final answer.
evals.expected_output: Recover and report the retained answer without rerunning the review.
expectations: Matches the settled result to the interrupted request
Drains retained output and returns the existing answer
Does not send a continuation or replay prompt just because the observer failed
Audits retained tool calls and effects and checks the original goal before returning the answer

evals.name: partial-work-before-resume
evals.prompt: An authorized aopus -w task failed after editing two files. The saved session matches, the request settled as failed, and a previous checkout snapshot and tool log are available.
evals.expected_output: Audit partial effects and remaining work, then continue the verified conversation.
expectations: Inspects actual file changes and tool calls before deciding what remains
Writes a continuation describing verified completed work, remaining work, and the current permission scope
Uses the same named session with fresh prompt/log files and no automatic prompt retries for recovery
Verifies backend ID/model/thinking afterward and preserves earlier receipts and logs

evals.name: unknown-external-effect
evals.prompt: The queue owner died after a delegated task attempted an authorized external operation. There is no turn_result and no receipt proving whether the operation completed.
evals.expected_output: Report the uncertain outcome and preserve the session; no automatic retry of the operation.
expectations: Does not treat owner death or missing output as proof that the operation did not happen
Seeks independent evidence of the external effect
Leaves the dependent retry pending if the outcome remains unknown
Does not create a new session or blindly replay the original prompt

evals.name: first-turn-failed-receipt
evals.prompt: The first prompt in a new ACPX session crashed before any completed reply. Pick up the task using the launch receipt.
evals.expected_output: Use metadata saved before the first prompt to verify the session and classify the interrupted request.
expectations: Expects a private receipt saved after ensure and before the first prompt
Compares backend IDs; distinguishes a proven empty first-start replacement from losing an established task, and does not infer continuity from the local record alone
Classifies the existing request and audits any effects before deciding whether to continue

evals.name: closed-session-no-replacement
evals.prompt: Continue review session auth. Its exact-cwd record matches the saved model but has closed true; a same-named active session exists in a parent directory.
evals.expected_output: Report the closed task session; do not continue in the ancestor or create a replacement.
expectations: Checks closed state and exact cwd/record identity
Does not run ensure, new, or prompt against the ancestor session

evals.name: expired-guard-preserves-scope
evals.prompt: Pick up our interrupted aopus task. Its saved guarded command has expired and the adapter is no longer running. A refresh could change the selection digest.
evals.expected_output: Inspect retained evidence with the original scope and report that continuation is blocked by the guard.
expectations: Uses saved command for metadata/history/watch/cancel as needed
Does not refresh global routing, append allow-stale, or substitute a new command to resume
Reports the current routing-helper limitation without claiming the retained session guarantees resumability

evals.name: request-id-after-observer-crash
evals.prompt: The shell died before saving its after-prompt snapshot. The text log has no request ID. We were the only submitter to this task session.
evals.expected_output: Recover lastRequestId from current metadata and correlate it with the prompt and watch lifecycle events.
expectations: Does not claim the text prompt log contains a request ID
Uses lastRequestId and submitted prompt/events to establish the target request
Stops if correlation remains ambiguous
If lastRequestId is a raw JSON-RPC ID with no turn_started match, uses a uniquely correlated lifecycle event after the last settled boundary; otherwise reports unknown

evals.name: watcher-terminal-error
evals.prompt: Our managed recovery watcher returned WATCH_CURSOR_EXPIRED before we found the target turn_result.
evals.expected_output: Stop the watcher and preserve an unknown outcome while inspecting other evidence.
expectations: Stops the watcher by its managed task handle and drains its log
Does not treat cursor expiry as task failure or permission to resubmit
Inspects retained logs and effects before further action

evals.name: user-cancel-stop
evals.prompt: I cancelled the delegated task. ACPX cancel returned cancel requested, and the original prompt is still running.
evals.expected_output: Wait for a settled cancellation, audit effects, and stop without automatically continuing.
expectations: Confirms through done cancelled or the target request turn_result, not the cancel response alone
Audits effects and reports the settled result
Stops pending renewed user direction; does not submit a continuation

evals.name: claude-shell-state
evals.prompt: Launch a new external review from Claude Code using the canonical shell example.
evals.expected_output: Run the complete setup, creation, prompt, and snapshot block in one managed background shell task.
expectations: Does not put only the final prompt line in a new shell with undefined variables
Keeps the task handle and relays bounded log chunks
Retains both receipts and the prompt exit status
A failed after-snapshot is reported for recovery without replacing the prompt exit status
